# Todos, reflection, and shortlisting

These are **Orchestrator** knobs — they change how CugaLite plans and retries, not which tools you attach.

<Callout type="info">
**Architecture:** Reflection and todos run inside the agent loop. The configured shortlister selects tools for `find_tools` and provider binding when the tool catalog is large. See [How CUGA works](/docs/start/how-it-works#3-capability-layer).
</Callout>

All three live under `[advanced_features]` in `settings.toml`.

---

## Todos

Off by default. When on, CugaLite gets a `create_update_todos` tool and prompt instructions so it can keep a checklist for multi-step work (and reset it between tasks).

```toml
[advanced_features]
enable_todos = true
```

Use it when a task has several independent steps you want the model to track. Leave it off for short, single-tool runs.

---

## Reflection

Off by default. After a sandbox/code step, CUGA checks whether the result actually moved the task forward. If not, it can retry instead of answering from a bad state.

```toml
[advanced_features]
reflection_enabled = true
```

Turn it on when wrong-but-confident answers are costly. Leave it off when latency matters more than a second look.

---

## Pre-execute VERIFY

VERIFY inspects a proposed mutating code block before the sandbox runs it. It is independent of post-execution reflection and defaults to off:

```toml
[advanced_features]
pre_execute_verify_enabled = true
pre_execute_verify_timeout = 60
```

Read-only blocks skip the check. A `revise` decision skips the proposed block so the agent can revise it; `ok` or `unknown` allows execution. Errors/timeouts fail open, and revision caps prevent endless verification loops. VERIFY is an advisory LLM check, not human approval or a deterministic authorization boundary. Use [Tool Approval](/docs/build/policies/tool-approval) and [ToolGuard](/docs/build/policies/tool-guard) for their respective controls.

## Tool shortlister (`find_tools`)

When an app has **more tools than the threshold**, CugaLite does not dump the whole catalog into the prompt. It exposes **`find_tools`**: the model describes what it needs in natural language, and the configured **shortlister** returns the relevant subset.

```toml
[advanced_features]
shortlisting_tool_threshold = 35   # find_tools when total tools > this
cuga_lite_enable_few_shots = true  # few-shots for the shortlister path
```

### Shortlisting strategies

| Strategy | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `llm` | Ask the model to choose tools; default. |
| `embedding` | Rank tools with local cosine similarity without an LLM call. |
| `hybrid` | Prefilter with cosine similarity, then ask the LLM for the final selection. |
| Dotted class path | Load a custom shortlister implementation. |

```toml
[shortlister]
strategy = "hybrid"
fallback_strategy = "llm"
threshold = 128
top_k = 128
max_results = 10
min_score = 0.15
embedding_provider = "local"
embedding_model = "BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5"
```

`advanced_features.shortlisting_tool_threshold` decides when the prompt hides tools behind `find_tools`. `[shortlister].threshold` decides when the cosine stage engages. Shortlister embeddings are local by default and do not inherit `[storage.embedding]`. Use `[shortlister.discovery]` and `[shortlister.bind_cap]` for separate runtime-discovery and provider-cap overrides.

See the [shortlister design and extension guide](https://github.com/cuga-project/cuga-agent/blob/main/docs/design/pluggable-shortlister.md) for custom implementations.

Over-cap on **native** `bind_tools` (providers that reject > ~128 tools) uses the configured shortlister:

```toml
[advanced_features]
cuga_lite_bind_tools_max_count = 128   # 0 disables the cap
cuga_lite_bind_tools_pad_to_cap = false
cuga_lite_bind_tools_include_find_tools = false
```
